471	(`subcanonical_etaleTopology`, absent from Mathlib `v4.31` for the étale
472	topology but free from `proetaleTopology`), and
473	`picSharp_representableBy_picEt_transport` transports a `picSharp`
474	representation to a `picEt` one with **no** rational-point hypothesis, the same
475	scheme serving both. So no supplementary étale-representability theorem is
476	needed.
477	
478	**What the correction costs instead, and it is a sharper constraint.**
479	Representability of `picSharp` over an arbitrary field is **FALSE**, so **G3 and
480	G4 target a false statement as written**, not a hard one. The source says so
481	directly: Kleiman L5105–L5108 on the conic `u²+v²+w²=0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — smooth,
482	proper, geometrically integral, no rational point — `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not
483	representable while `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is.
484	
485	**This does not go through the Zariski-sheaf theorem, and an earlier revision of
486	this paragraph wrongly said it did** (`I-0970`). The Lean statement
487	`PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy` is true and useful, but
488	its contrapositive needs "`picSharp` is not a Zariski sheaf", which no source
489	here establishes — `ex:Pfs` compares the two *sheafifications*, and `th:cmp`
490	part 1 shows `picSharp ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` on these binders, so it is
491	Zariski-*separated*. The route that does work is
492	`not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso` (see the sheafification paragraph
493	above): comparison-failure alone refutes representability, with no topology in
494	the argument. Everything through J5 runs over a separably closed
495	`k'` where a section is available and the obstruction absent; the break is the
496	descent step where the conclusion returns to `k`, and the repair is that the
497	object descended must be `picEt` (which has the sheaf property that carries
498	descent) rather than `picSharp`. Over `k'` the two agree. Restating G3/G4 that
499	way reaches clause (1) with no false intermediate.
500	
501	Not formalised, and named as such: that Kleiman's non-sheaf curve satisfies this
502	file's binders (smooth, proper, geometrically integral) is quoted from the
503	reference rather than proved. Tracked as `AJC.picrep.etale-rep`; the board node
504	`AJC.picrep` carries the landed/absent split.
505	
506	**How many inputs the repair has, and which are now in hand** — the count has
507	moved twice, so it is stated here as a history rather than as a fact.
508	"Descend `picEt` instead of `picSharp`" was priced at two inputs (2026-07-29
509	`ajc-p1`), then three (`review-ajc`, adding the cross-base identification), and
510	is now **four** (`review-ajc`, `I-1135`, adding the section over separably closed
511	fields that everything else silently assumes) — **plus a fifth entry added
512	2026-07-30 which is a subtraction, not an input**: all four price the
513	`RepresentableBy` field of clause (1), and the *other two fields of that same
514	clause* are free (item 5 below, `I-1286`).
515	
516	**And a list of inputs is not a route — corrected 2026-07-30 (`ajc-p2`), because
517	for four rounds this paragraph was one.** Every entry below is an *antecedent*.
518	There is **still** no declaration anywhere in this project stating the theorem they
519	are antecedents *of*, and an earlier revision of this paragraph — written by the
520	lane that added `Picard/PicEtDescentAssembly.lean` — claimed that file supplied
521	one. **It does not** (refuted by a fresh-context audit, `I-1312`, reproduced and
522	accepted by its author): none of that file's declarations takes a `k'`-side
523	representation and concludes over `k`. Its
524	`representableByRestrict_of_baseChange` concludes a `RepresentableBy` for a
525	`k'`-**object**, i.e. it restates the `k'`-side input in the right variables rather
526	than crossing the descent step. The census below is accurate; the remedy is not
527	applied. The conclusion shape
528	`Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X)` occurred at exactly three sites
529	— the `HasPicSchemeEt` class field and the seam `sorry` below, plus
530	`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` — and all three are **same-field**,
531	none taking a representation over a larger field and concluding over `k`
532	(measured by `ajc-p2`, re-measured independently by `review-ajc`, `I-1256`). With
533	the goal unwritten, an input nobody held would not have shown up as missing.
534	
535	What *is* settled, and it is a pricing fact rather than a step: do **not** budget
536	effectivity of `picEt`-**classes** along the field-extension cover. Both halves are
537	free from sheafification — `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` already says so in prose at
538	its own §4 (`:289`, `:294`: "unique amalgamation", "every covering sieve, `⊤`
539	included, free from sheafification"), and `PicEtDescentAssembly.lean`'s
540	`existsUnique_amalgamation_picEt_fieldCover` is that lemma `rfl`-equal, proposition
541	and term (`I-1312`). Its `picEt_injective_restrict_baseTest` is the
542	sieve-to-single-morphism reduction; that step is unavoidable, but it is **not
543	geometric** — the same statement closes in an arbitrary category with pullbacks,
544	with every geometric hypothesis deleted (`I-1312`, `I-1316`). So what remains is the
545	invariance step producing a compatible family from a Galois-**invariant** `k'`-class
546	(`G1`, where the group action enters), the **scheme-level** quotient (`G2`, item 3),
547	and `k'`-side representability itself. `I-1280` states the pricing consequence and
548	`I-1312` corrects that item's overclaims.
549	
550	Present state of the four:
551	
552	1. **the descent test — LANDED.** `Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` proves
553	   `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k` is an étale cover for `k'/k` finite separable and that
554	   `picEt` satisfies the sheaf axiom at that cover.
555	2. **the cross-base identification — CLOSED** (`Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean`,
556	   `PicScheme.picEt_crossBaseIso`, `sorry`-free and axiom-clean). Without it the
557	   scheme `J5` produces over `k'` would represent `picEt` *of the curve over `k`,
558	   restricted to `k'`-tests* rather than `picEt` of the base-changed curve, and
559	   there would be no functor for the descent datum to be a datum *for* — a
560	   mismatch no green build would reveal. **Note the hypotheses it does NOT
561	   carry**: earlier revisions of this paragraph, and the board row, both stated
562	   the obligation for `k'/k` *finite separable*; the theorem needs neither
563	   hypothesis and holds for an arbitrary field extension, because the argument is
564	   about pullback projections rather than about étale covers. Finite-separability
565	   is item 1's constraint and was double-counted here. Do not budget a
566	   separability argument for a cross-base step.
567	3. **the Galois action and quotient — G1/G2, substantially built; the gate now
568	   bites only off the affine locus.** Updated 2026-07-30 (`ajc-p1`): the class
569	   `AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.HasGaloisQuotient` is **no longer
570	   instance-free**. `hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine`
571	   (`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`, global `instance`, `sorry`-free and

573	   theorem) discharges it for **every** semilinear action on an affine total
574	   space — not just for the affine *model* `specSemilinearGalAction`, which is
575	   what `isGaloisQuotient_spec` had covered. The step was
576	   `isGaloisQuotient_congr`, transport of `IsGaloisQuotient` along an equivariant
577	   isomorphism over `Spec L`, applied to `X.isoSpec`; it subsumes the former
578	   single-object witness `hasGaloisQuotient_specF4` by `inferInstance`.
579	   **What this does not do, and it is the part that matters for this seam**: the
580	   campaign consumer `J'_r` is a *glued* scheme, hence non-affine, and
581	   `inferInstance` for the gate at an abstract action carrying the orbit
582	   hypothesis but not affineness **fails** (measured, control both ways). So the
583	   remaining `G2(c)` work is exactly the `Scheme.GlueData` assembly of the

603	   and would read as absence. That is the recorded "cited names need `#check`,
604	   not `grep`" trap; import that module before probing either class.

627	   **The stronger claim first published here — that they were "never mentioned"
628	   anywhere — is FALSE and is withdrawn** (`review-ajc`, corrected by a

633	   `hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` ("the local-finiteness and
634	   separatedness conjuncts are carried across unchanged, because the transport
635	   does not move the representing scheme"). What is genuinely new here is a
636	   *different* route — free from a bare `picEt` representation, with no `picSharp`
637	   detour — and the descent-unavailability fact below. That distinction is
638	   load-bearing: on the **field-descent** route this board actually holds, the
639	   transport argument is not available, so there the two conjuncts really were
640	   live and unpriced. So **clause (1) is now a two-field obligation**, and a
641	   lane closing the descent step should target
642	   `seamClauseOne_of_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType`. Measured, `lake env
643	   lean` EXIT=0, axiom-clean against a control that fires `sorryAx` here:
644	   * `LocallyOfFiniteType` **descends** across the cover. At `k'/k` with

646	     `Spec.map (algebraMap k k')` is `Surjective`, `Flat` and `QuasiCompact` all

648	     `DescendsAlong @LocallyOfFiniteType (@Surjective ⊓ @Flat ⊓ @QuasiCompact)`
649	     (`Morphisms/LocalFlatDescent.lean`) then closes it via
650	     `of_pullback_fst_of_descendsAlong`.
651	   * `IsSeparated` **cannot** descend with Mathlib `v4.31` — and does not need

655	     (`IsClosedImmersion` is not a `HasRingHomProperty`, so
656	     `HasRingHomProperty.descendsAlong_flat` does not apply).
657	     **So do not budget a separatedness-descent argument: the lemma it would cite
658	     does not exist.** (A previous revision of this sentence added "Mathlib has

662	     `Morphisms/FlatDescent.lean` registers six more, all of which synthesise on
663	     probe: `Surjective`, `UniversallyClosed`, `UniversallyOpen`,
664	     `UniversallyInjective`, `isomorphisms Scheme`, `IsOpenImmersion` — eleven,
665	     not five. It was one file's count published as Mathlib's, three lines below
666	     this file's own method note warning about exactly that. The absence of the
667	     two properties above is unaffected: it was measured by failed synthesis, not
668	     inferred from any list. Do not quote a total here; grep
669	     `DescendsAlong` and count.) Separatedness instead comes from the *group structure of
670	     the represented object*: `picEt` is `CommGrpCat`-valued (`picEtCommGrp`), so
671	     ANY scheme representing it is a group object over `Spec k` by Yoneda
672	     transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy _ (picEtCommGrp C)
673	     (rep.ofIso (picEtCommGrpForgetIso C))`), and a group scheme over a field is
674	     separated. From a bare `(PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X` this is a
675	     theorem — it does not even use `[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]`.
676	   **BOTH ARE NOW LANDED, 2026-07-30 (`ajc-p1`), in
677	   `Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`** — so this item is no longer a costing, and the
678	   sentence that stood here ("the one brick is a **port** … none of those three
679	   names exists in this project") is false at HEAD and replaced. Mathlib still
680	   does not have "group scheme over a field is separated" (re-measured both ways
681	   in one probe: `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left` synthesises for `[GrpObj G]` over
682	   `Spec K` while `IsSeparated G.hom` does **not**), and the argument is
683	   transcribed from `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`'s
684	   `AbelianVariety/GroupSeparated.lean`; all three names now exist here.
685	   * field 3: `isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt` — `IsSeparated X.hom` from a
686	     bare `(PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X`, arbitrary field, and
687	     `seamClauseOne_of_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType` restates clause (1) as
688	     the **two-field** obligation. Aim a descent step at *that*.
689	   * field 2: `locallyOfFiniteType_of_baseChange` — the descent above, carried
690	     out, so the contrast is compiler-checked rather than asserted. **The two side
691	     conjuncts are free for opposite reasons**, which is the part a costing gets
692	     wrong: one is a descent argument and the other is free precisely because
693	     descent is unavailable for it. Field 2 descends at an **arbitrary** field
694	     extension: its theorem formerly carried `[Algebra.IsSeparable k k']` and
695	     `[Module.Finite k k']` and consumed neither, and both are now deleted
696	     (`I-1356`). Finite separability is **input 1's** price —
697	     `picEt_ext_of_pullback_agrees` genuinely needs it — so this is the *same*
698	     double-count the input-2 note below corrects, and it was live in two files.
699	   Both `sorry`-free and axiom-clean against this theorem as a control; gate-free
700	   (no `HasPicSchemeEt` binder on any of them, checked by full signature per
701	   `I-1292`, not by header). Non-vacuity measured: dropping `rep` leaves
702	   `IsSeparated X.hom` for an arbitrary `X` and `infer_instance` **fails**.
703	   **This is not a discount on the seam**: `k'`-side representability is still
704	   the campaign's undischarged output, and field 1 is witnessed for no curve. It
705	   removes two obligations nobody had counted, and forecloses one dead end.
706	
707	Method note for whoever re-checks any absence claim in this area: a bare
708	`horizon search picEt` returns ten hits, **all from the sibling project**, because
709	the result set is capped — reading that as absence in AJC would be a false
710	negative. Query a specific name (`picEtComparison`) or scan declaration headers
711	in-tree. Two earlier revisions of this paragraph offered lists called "the
712	complete list" and **both were wrong** (`I-1075`, and a fresh-context audit that
713	found six omissions); neither error touched the conclusion, which is why a token
714	scan rather than a census is what such a claim should rest on.
715	
716	Item 2 was **not** portable from the sibling project, which was the trap, and the
717	outcome recorded it: `AJCR` proves a cross-base comparison as a `MulEquiv`
718	(`picEtCrossBaseEquiv`, `Picard/PicEtCrossBase.lean:316`, 468 lines), but its
719	`picEt` is a hand-built affine-opens limit of plus-classes (`PicEt.lean:105`)
720	while this file's is a categorical sheafification (`PicEtSheaf.lean:238`) —
721	different objects, no `lake` edge. Most of that length is a section-ring scalar
722	tower which a *sheafification*-based `picEt` does not need, because for it the
723	whole sheafification layer collapses to one Mathlib lemma
724	(`Functor.pushforwardContinuousSheafificationCompatibility`, applicable because
725	restriction along `Over.map` is continuous for the two localised étale topologies
726	by pure synthesis). Reading the sibling as a design lead rather than transcribing
727	it was the cheaper move.
728	
729	This is the **sole** `sorry` of the seam: everything else below — the
730	representing scheme `PicSchemeEt`, its representability, local finiteness,
731	separatedness and group-scheme structure, the comparison theorem
732	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and the conditional
733	`picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from it.
734	
735	**Why the second conjunct is bundled here rather than given its own `sorry`.**
736	Clause (1) is Kleiman §4; clause (2) is Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (`th:comp`): given a
737	section, the comparison `picSharp C → Pic_{(C/k)ét}` is an isomorphism. Both are
738	theorems of the same paper and neither is formalised. They are stated as one
739	named obligation on purpose: the `picSharp`-shaped consumer interface
740	(`HasPicScheme`, and through it the tangent-space chain and the `k̄` Albanese
741	witness) needs clause (2) to exist at all, and splitting it out would report the
742	Jacobian headline as resting on *six* open obligations where the mathematics has
743	five. The bundling adds no strength — clause (2) is conditional on a section, so
744	it says nothing about a pointless curve — and it keeps the frontier count honest
745	in both directions. `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` measures the result rather
746	than asserting it.
747	
748	**"Adds no strength" is now MEASURED, and the measurement is sharper than the
749	claim** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30; `lake env lean` EXIT=0 in a scratch file,
750	since deleted). Both conjuncts of this theorem follow, *together*, from the
751	single hypothesis
752	
753	  `∃ X, Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp C).RepresentableBy X) ∧`
754	  `      LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom`
755	
756	— i.e. from the `picSharp`-shaped endpoint that the Milne–Kollár campaign's ten
757	modules are built to produce, with **nothing left over**. Clause (1) is
758	`hasPicSchemeEt_of_picSharp_representability` and clause (2) is
759	`isIso_picEtComparison_of_picSharp_representability` (both
760	`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`), the second discarding the section it is handed.
761	Axiom-clean `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`. The two halves existed
762	separately; what had not been measured is that their conjunction is exactly this
763	statement, so no reader had to take "adds no strength" on trust.
764	
765	**The control here has a trap in it, and the trap is worth more than the
766	result.** The obvious control — "does the conclusion close *without* the campaign
767	hypothesis?" — **succeeds**, so read naively it says the reduction is empty.
768	`exact?` closes clause (1) hypothesis-free via
769	`HasPicSchemeEt.has_pic_scheme_et`, and clause (2) via
770	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`. Both are legitimate terms; both
771	route through `instHasPicSchemeEt`, which *is* a projection of the `sorry` below.
772	Measured: the hypothesis-free version reports
773	`[propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` while the version above
774	reports no `sorryAx`. So on this seam **provability is not a discriminating
775	control and the axiom list is** — because an unconditional gate instance makes
776	every statement in its domain provable. Anyone probing a reduction anywhere near
777	`HasPicSchemeEt` should compare axiom lists, not success and failure.
778	
779	**What this does NOT mean, since it is the natural misreading.** It does not
780	bring the seam closer. The hypothesis is the campaign's *undischarged output*,
781	and over an arbitrary `k` there is a refutation waiting for it —
782	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
783	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) turns any failure of
784	`IsIso (picEtComparison C)` into a refutation of the existential, and Kleiman's
785	pointless real conic is where that failure is expected.
786	
787	**Stated precisely, because the first version of this paragraph overstated it**
788	(`review-ajc`, corrected within the same session): that refutation is
789	*conditional* on `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)`, which is **quoted from Kleiman,

8	import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.Representability

10	/-!
11	# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)
12	
13	The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
14	honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
15	local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
16	degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
19	  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
20	  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
22	  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
24	  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
25	  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
26	  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
27	  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
28	  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
29	  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
30	  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
31	  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
32	  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
34	  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
35	  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
36	  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
37	  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
38	  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
39	  Σ-component of the universal element.
40	-/
41

45

47	
48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
49	
50	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
51	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
52	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
53	
54	/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/
55	
56	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
57	massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
58	noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
59	  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat
60	
61	@[simp]
62	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_obj (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
63	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj T = pic0Subgroup C T.unop :=
64	  rfl
65	
66	lemma pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ} (g : T ⟶ T')
67	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T.unop) :
68	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map g lam = pic0Map C g.unop lam :=
69	  rfl
70	
71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)
78	
79	variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
80	
81	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem
143	
144	/-- **The Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor, bundled as a sheaf on the
145	big Zariski site** — the object mathlib's 01JJ local-representability engine
146	consumes. -/
147	noncomputable def pic0SigmaSheaf : Sheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology.{u} (Type u) :=
148	  ⟨pic0SigmaFunctor C,
149	    (isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type _ _).mpr (pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf C)⟩
150

152	
153	/-- **The DAT-glue statement (worksheet §4, DAT-glue row)**: a chart family of
154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's
155	certificates) that is jointly Zariski-locally surjective (DAT-B's coverage) induces —
156	through mathlib's 01JJ engine and the stage-2 Σ-descent — a representation of the
157	type-valued degree-zero Picard functor by the glued scheme placed over the
158	Σ-component of the universal element.  The represented object's `.left` is
159	`(Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued` and its `.hom` is the universal
160	element's Σ-component, both definitionally. -/
161	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
162	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
163	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
164	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
165	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)] :
166	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
167	      (Over.mk ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
168	        (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1) :=
169	  (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).overSlice
170

########## Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity 80-125

This is dat-b row B-5 verbatim — "every `pic⁰` point is Zariski-locally a chart point" — with
one deliberate design choice: the sieve is described through the individual `f i`, so a
producer discharges it by exhibiting, for each point of `T`, one open neighbourhood and one
index.  It never has to mention `Sigma.desc` or the coproduct of yoneda presheaves.  Turning
that into the coproduct form is `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc` below. -/
def ChartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)),
    (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T

/-- **B-6**: the coverage hypothesis gives the local-surjectivity instance that
`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes.

The proof is the bookkeeping the row's name hides: the image sieve of `Sigma.desc f` contains
the image sieve of every individual `f i` — because a `T'`-point of `X i` gives a `T'`-point
of the coproduct through `Sigma.ι` — hence contains their supremum, and a sieve containing a
covering sieve is covering.

Note what is *not* needed: no compatibility between charts, and no injectivity.  `Sigma.desc`
imposes no coherence condition across indices (the observation `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`
makes for `hf`, here again for coverage), so a heterogeneous atlas is admissible for B-6 on
exactly the same footing as a homogeneous one. -/
theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) :
    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) where
  imageSieve_mem {T} s := by
    refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_ (h T s)
    refine iSup_le fun i => ?_
    rintro T' g ⟨t, ht⟩
    -- transport the witness along `Sigma.ι` and use `Sigma.ι_desc`
    refine ⟨(Sigma.ι (fun j => yoneda.obj (X j)) i).app (op T') t, ?_⟩
    rw [← ht, ← NatTrans.comp_app_apply, Sigma.ι_desc f i]

/-- **The hypothesis is satisfiable, checked rather than assumed.**

If one chart of the family is surjective on the points of every test, the coverage hypothesis
holds — its image sieve is already the maximal sieve.  This is the degenerate case (and not
the geometric situation: no single Abel chart is surjective on all tests), but it rules out
the failure mode where a `Prop`-valued hypothesis turns out to be unsatisfiable and the
"reduction" above is therefore vacuous.

Compare the two-sided check in `Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`: there the question was whether the
datum was too *weak*; here it is whether it is too *strong*. -/
theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_forall_surjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (i : ι)
    (hi : ∀ T : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ, Function.Surjective ((f i).app T)) :
    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
  intro T s
  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.superset_covering ?_

/-! ## The affine-opens limit -/

variable (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))

/-- The compatible families over the affine opens of the test object, as a subgroup of
the product of the affine-level plus groups: the value at a smaller affine open is the
restriction of the value at a larger one. -/
def picEtSubgroup :
    Subgroup (Π U : T.left.affineOpens, PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1)) where
  carrier := {s | ∀ (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1),
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s V) = s U}
  one_mem' := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.one_apply, Pi.one_apply, map_one]
  mul_mem' {a b} ha hb := fun U V h => by
    rw [Pi.mul_apply, Pi.mul_apply, map_mul, ha U V h, hb U V h]
  inv_mem' {a} ha := fun U V h => by rw [Pi.inv_apply, Pi.inv_apply, map_inv, ha U V h]

/-- **The étale-sheafified relative Picard functor at an arbitrary test object**, object
level: compatible families of affine-level plus classes over the affine opens of
`T.left` — the bespoke affine-opens limit of `PicEtAff C ∘ Γ(T.left, ·)`.  On affine
tests this is `PicEtAff` itself (`picEtAffineEquiv`); on general tests it is its
canonical Zariski-continuous extension. -/
def picEt : Type u :=
  picEtSubgroup C T

noncomputable instance : CommGroup (picEt C T) :=
  inferInstanceAs (CommGroup (picEtSubgroup C T))

namespace picEt

variable {C T}

/-- The compatibility of a section of `picEt` along an inclusion of affine opens. -/
lemma compat (s : picEt C T) (U V : T.left.affineOpens) (h : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
    PicEtAff.mapAlg C (Over.resAlgHom T h) (s.1 V) = s.1 U :=
  s.2 U V h

@[ext]
lemma ext {s t : picEt C T} (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, s.1 U = t.1 U) : s = t :=
  Subtype.ext (funext h)

variable (C T) in
/-- Evaluation of a section of `picEt` at an affine open, as a group homomorphism. -/
def eval (U : T.left.affineOpens) : picEt C T →* PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, U.1) :=
  (Pi.evalMonoidHom (fun V : T.left.affineOpens => PicEtAff C Γ(T.left, V.1)) U).comp
    (picEtSubgroup C T).subtype

########## AJC PicEtSheaf.lean 200-280
object, stated separately because it is the property consumers cite: a
representing scheme for `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` exists only because the functor being
represented is an étale sheaf (a representable functor is a sheaf for any
subcanonical topology, so a non-sheaf can never be representable — which is
exactly why the unsheafified `relPresheaf` needs a rational point).

Proved, not assumed: sheafification produces a sheaf. -/
theorem etaleSheaf_isSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
  (etaleSheaf C).property

/-- **The comparison map** `Pic_{C/k} ⟶ Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, i.e. the unit of the
sheafification adjunction at the relative Picard presheaf.

Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5 (`th:comp`) says this map is an isomorphism when `C` has a
`k`-rational point (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic here). Over an
arbitrary base field it is only a comparison: the honest object is the target,
which is why the representability obligation is stated there. -/
noncomputable def toEtaleSheaf {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ (etaleSheaf C).obj :=
  CategoryTheory.toSheafify (etaleTopologyOver k) (PicSharp.relPresheaf C)

/-- The universal property of the sheafification, in the form consumers use:
every morphism from the relative Picard presheaf to (the underlying presheaf
of) an étale sheaf factors uniquely through `toEtaleSheaf`.

This is what makes `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` the *canonical* choice rather than one
sheaf among many, and it is the step that turns a representing scheme for the
sheaf into a universal receiver of relative Picard classes. -/
noncomputable def etaleSheafHomEquiv {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    (G : Sheaf (etaleTopologyOver k) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    (etaleSheaf C ⟶ G) ≃ (PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⟶ G.obj) :=
  ((CategoryTheory.sheafificationAdjunction (etaleTopologyOver k)
    AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).homEquiv (PicSharp.relPresheaf C) G)

end PicSharp

namespace PicScheme

/-! ## §3. The set-valued functor that gets represented -/

/-- **The functor whose representability is the project's central obligation**:
the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor with its group structure
forgotten,

Contrast with `picSharp C = relPresheaf C ⋙ forget`: that functor is
representable only under a rational-point hypothesis (it is not even a
Zariski sheaf otherwise), whereas *this* one is the object of Kleiman §4
Thm. `th:main` and its representability needs no hypothesis on `C(k)`. -/
noncomputable def picEt {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] :
    (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1) :=
  (PicSharp.etaleSheaf C).obj ⋙ CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}

/-- The comparison `picSharp C ⟶ picEt C` of set-valued functors, the
set-level shadow of `PicSharp.toEtaleSheaf`. An isomorphism under a
`k`-rational point (Kleiman §2 Thm. 2.5), a comparison in general.

The source is written out as `PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget _` rather than as

not proved in this project** — `PicEtSubcanonical.lean` says so itself, and

quantify over it as a hypothesis.

Unlike the legacy `HasPicScheme`, this class carries **no** hypothesis on

carrier of the project's central open obligation.

**It is not a gate, and quantifying over it does not keep a consumer
kernel-clean** — the previous sentence here promised that and it is
undeliverable (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-29). Because `instHasPicSchemeEt` is
unconditional, instance search discharges this class for every object in its own
domain, so a consumer that binds it is `sorryAx`-reachable the moment it is
applied; there is no `C` in the domain for which the binder is a real
restriction. Contrast `HasPicScheme`, which has no instance at all and for which
the binder genuinely is a hypothesis. What this class does buy is the shape:
statements quantified over it read as implications and are stated for an
arbitrary base field, per `I-0491`. See `PicSchemeEt` below for the

    (t' : overSpec k K ⟶ T') :
    degAt ((picEtFunctor C).map f.op lam) t' = degAt lam (t' ≫ f) :=
  degAt_picEtMap f lam t'

end DegAt

/-! ## The degree-zero subfunctor -/

variable (C) in
/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
    degAt lam t = 0}
  one_mem' := by
    intro K _ _ t
    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by
    intro a b ha hb K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by
    intro a ha K _ _ t
    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

/-- Membership in the degree-zero subgroup: degree zero at every field point. -/
theorem mem_pic0Subgroup_iff {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} :
    lam ∈ pic0Subgroup C T
      ↔ ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),
          degAt lam t = 0 :=
  Iff.rfl

variable (C) in
/-- Restriction of degree-zero classes along a morphism of test objects: the map part
of the degree-zero Picard functor.  The stability of the degree-zero condition is
definitional through the functoriality `degAt_picEtMap` of the degree at field
points. -/
def pic0Map {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) :
    pic0Subgroup C T →* pic0Subgroup C T' :=
  ((picEtMap C f).comp (pic0Subgroup C T).subtype).codRestrict (pic0Subgroup C T')

naturality square of the subfunctor inclusion, element form. -/

theorem pic0Map_coe {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T)
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C T) :

  rfl

/-- **The degree-zero relative Picard functor `Pic⁰_{C/k}`** (gap G-D7): the subgroup
subfunctor of the étale-sheafified relative Picard functor `picEtFunctor C` of classes
of degree zero at every field point of the test object.  This is the binding carrier of

functor. -/
def pic0Functor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} where
  obj T := CommGrpCat.of (pic0Subgroup C T.unop)
  map g := CommGrpCat.ofHom (pic0Map C g.unop)

    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z : picEt C T.unop => z.1 U) (picEtMap_id C (lam : picEt C T.unop))
  map_comp g h := by
    ext lam U
    exact congrArg (fun z => z.1 U) (picEtMap_comp C g.unop h.unop (lam : picEt C _))

### AJCR: RepresentableBy occurrences on picEtFunctor (full Pic)

### AJCR JacobianDataCharts 100-230
section Charts

variable {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
  (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)

/-- **The structure morphism of the `i`-th chart** over the base field: the Σ-component of the
element of `pic0SigmaFunctor C` classified by `f i`.  A chart of the degree-zero Picard sheaf
is by construction a scheme *together with* a map to `Spec k`, namely the base over which the
line bundle it classifies lives; this is that map. -/
noncomputable def chartHom (i : ι) : X i ⟶ Spec (.of k) := (yonedaEquiv (f i)).1

variable (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (f i))
variable [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]

/-- **The structure morphism of the glued object of a chart family**: mathlib's 01JJ engine
glues the charts into a scheme representing the Σ-extension sheaf, and the Σ-component of the
universal element of that representation is the map of that scheme to `Spec k`. -/
noncomputable abbrev gluedHom :
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued ⟶ Spec (.of k) :=
  ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
    (𝟙 (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued)).1

/-- **The glued object of a chart family**, as a scheme over the base field.  This is the
object represented by `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`. -/
noncomputable abbrev gluedOfCharts : Over (Spec (.of k)) := Over.mk (gluedHom C f hf)

/-- The universal element of the glued representation restricts along the `i`-th glue map to
the element classified by `f i`. -/
lemma representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued (i : ι) :
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv
      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i) = yonedaEquiv (f i) :=
  Scheme.LocalRepresentability.yonedaGluedToSheaf_app_toGlued hf

/-- **The charts are charts over the base field**: the `i`-th glue map into the glued object,
followed by the structure morphism of the glued object, is the structure morphism of the `i`-th
chart.  Both sides are Σ-components of the same restriction of the universal element. -/
lemma toGlued_comp_gluedHom (i : ι) :
    Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i ≫ gluedHom C f hf = chartHom C f i := by
  have h := congrArg Sigma.fst
    ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy hf).homEquiv_eq
      (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.toGlued hf i))
  rw [representableBy_homEquiv_toGlued] at h
  exact h.symm

/-! ## The two finiteness certificates from the charts -/

/-- **Locally of finite type descends from the charts**: the property is local on the source
and the glue maps of the glue data cover the glued object, so if each chart is locally of finite
type over the base field then so is the glued object. -/
theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i)) :
    LocallyOfFiniteType (gluedHom C f hf) := by
  refine IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover
    (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType) (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover fun i => ?_
  have h := hlft i
  rwa [← toGlued_comp_gluedHom C f hf i] at h

/-- **Quasi-compactness descends from a finite family of quasi-compact charts**: the base
`Spec k` is affine, so quasi-compactness of the structure morphism is compactness of the space
of the glued object, and that space is the union of the finitely many compact chart images. -/
theorem quasiCompact_gluedHom [Finite ι] (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    QuasiCompact (gluedHom C f hf) := by
  haveI : Finite (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.I₀ := ‹Finite ι›
  haveI : ∀ i, CompactSpace ((Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.X i) := hcpt
  haveI : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued :=
    (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace
  exact HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›

/-! ## The producer -/

/-- **The first producer of the Jacobian datum**: a Zariski chart family of relatively
representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf of the degree-zero Picard functor,
jointly locally surjective, indexed by a finite type, with quasi-compact charts that are locally
of finite type over the base field, produces the pinned representability datum of the curve.

The representing object is the glued scheme of the family, placed over `Spec k` by the
Σ-component of the universal element; the two certificates are `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom`
and `quasiCompact_gluedHom`. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofCharts [Finite ι]
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    JacobianData C :=
  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
    (quasiCompact_gluedHom C f hf hcpt)

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofCharts_J [Finite ι]
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : ∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)) :
    (JacobianData.ofCharts C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
  rfl

/-- **The producer for an infinite atlas**: same as `JacobianData.ofCharts`, but the index type
is arbitrary and quasi-compactness of the glued object is supplied directly instead of being
derived from finitely many compact charts.

This is the form the classical construction needs.  The charts of the degree-zero Picard functor
are indexed by divisor *classes* — one chart per class whose twisted fibre class has an effective
witness — and that index set is not finite; compactness of the glued object is then a genuine
theorem about the Jacobian (it is the union of the images of a *quasi-compact* divisor scheme
under the Abel map), not a consequence of finiteness of the atlas.  Note that the
locally-of-finite-type certificate still descends from the charts with no finiteness hypothesis
whatsoever: `locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom` never uses `Finite ι`. -/
noncomputable def JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
    JacobianData C :=
  JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy C (gluedOfCharts C f hf)
    (pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C f hf)
    (locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom C f hf hlft)
    (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr hcpt)

@[simp]
lemma JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace_J
    (hlft : ∀ i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i))
    (hcpt : CompactSpace (Scheme.LocalRepresentability.glueData hf).glued) :
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfCompactSpace C f hf hlft hcpt).J = gluedOfCharts C f hf :=
  rfl

end Charts

theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),

THE PROJECTIVITY BRIDGE IS THE GAP BETWEEN KLEIMAN'S th:main AND THIS PROJECT'S CLAUSE (1), AND IT IS UNFORMALISED -- so "clause (1) is a theorem in the literature" (my own I-1360, flatly) needs the qualifier "for PROJECTIVE curves".

MEASURED by work-reviewer, fresh context, auditing my own r7 finding; reproduced and corrected in-file by me.

th:main's hypothesis (references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex L2155-L2157): f : X -> S "projective Zariski locally over S, and flat with integral geometric fibers". This project's binders: [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] over a field.

The bridge -- smooth proper curve over a field IS projective -- is classical mathematics and is NOT FORMALISED ANYWHERE IN AJC. No declaration combines projectivity with SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (searched, not grepped for a guessed name). The three sites that use the fact assert it as unproved prose: Picard/FlatteningStratification.lean:167, Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean:1345, Picard/Pic0Et.lean:190.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE IN I-1360. Unchanged: Kleiman's th:main really is clause (1)'s conclusion verbatim, with no rational-point hypothesis (quotation verified independently); its proof really does run Div via th:repDiv on the HILBERT scheme and descend by lm:qt (structure verified independently); so the seam's ORIGINAL docstring was naming the inputs of the published proof, and rejecting AJC.picrep.quot never rejected th:repDiv. Changed: reaching THIS FILE'S statement from th:main needs the projectivity bridge as a real, currently-absent input, so my sentence "clause (1) is a theorem in the literature; only its formalisation is open" was too strong as written.

AND IT SHARPENS THE PLANNING QUESTION rather than dissolving it. If Hilb-vs-Grassmannian for Div^d is priced, the Hilb side must include this bridge -- and note that three existing sites already need it and none pays for it, so it is owed on the current route too, not only on Kleiman's. That makes it a shared input rather than a cost of switching.

Corrected at the site: FGAPicRepresentability.lean's route block now says "clause (1) is known projectively, and the projectivity bridge is unformalised here" and tells readers not to cite it as "clause (1) is known".

9	# Galois quotient gluing, layer 1: the section-level semilinear action (campaign `G2(c)`)
10	
11	Let `L/K` be a finite Galois extension with group `Γ = Gal(L/K)` and let `X` be a
12	scheme over `Spec L` with a semilinear `Γ`-action `ρ` (`SemilinearGalAction`).  This
13	file opens the discharge of the last `G2` gate, `HasGaloisQuotient` (the gluing step
14	`G2(c)`), with the **overlap audit** (recorded below, before any Lean) and the first
15	construction layer.  **Update 2026-07-30:** layer 1 turned out to close the gate
16	outright for an **affine** `X` — `Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean` uses the
17	`U = ⊤` instance of the section action below, plus transport along `X.isoSpec`, to get
18	`hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine` as a global instance.  So the layers below are now
19	needed only for the **non-affine** case (the campaign's glued `J'_r`), and layer 3 may
20	quote a per-chart quotient instead of constructing one.  The first
21	construction layer: on every `Γ`-stable open `U` the action transports sections,
22	making `Γ(X, U)` an `L`-algebra with a semilinear `Γ`-action by ring automorphisms —
23	the section-level face of `SemilinearGalAction`, i.e. exactly the input format of the
24	affine quotient theorem `isGaloisQuotient_spec` — together with the scheme-level
25	restriction `ρ.restrict hU` of the action to `U` and the Spec-functoriality bridge
26	identifying the restricted action on an affine stable `U` with the `toSpecAut` action
27	of the section action under `hUa.isoSpec`.
28	
29	## MANDATORY OPENING AUDIT (milestone 0 — recorded before proving; the overlap pin)
30	
31	The glue construction needs the overlaps `U ⊓ V` of the stable affine cover to be
32	manageable.  `U ⊓ V` is always `Γ`-stable and open, but **need not be affine** when
33	`X` is not separated.  Verdicts on the two pinned resolutions:
34	
35	* **(a) Stable affine *basic*-open refinement with affine pairwise intersections: NOT
36	  extractable in general.**  Counterexample genus: the doubled affine plane
37	  `X = 𝔸²_L ⊔_{𝔸²_L ∖ 0} 𝔸²_L` (base change of the doubled plane over `K`, so it
38	  carries the canonical semilinear action; each chart is stable and trivially of
39	  `D(N)`-form, namely `D(1)` in itself).  *Any* two stable affine opens `U₁ ∋ o₁`,
40	  `U₂ ∋ o₂` around the two origins intersect in an open of `𝔸² ∖ 0` containing a
41	  punctured neighbourhood `V ∖ 0` of `0`, which is never affine (Hartogs:
42	  `Γ(V ∖ 0) = Γ(V)` in codimension `2`, so `V ∖ 0 → Spec Γ(V ∖ 0)` is not an open
43	  immersion at the missing point).  The chart-local identity `D(f) ∩ D(g) = D(fg)`
44	  is real but only applies *inside a common chart*; two `D(N)`s from different charts
45	  are exactly the doubled-plane situation.  So (a) is dead **as a route to affine
46	  overlaps**.
47	
48	* **However, affineness of the overlaps is NOT required** (this is the audit's main
49	  finding).  The classical construction (SGA I V.1.8; Mumford AV §7; Milne JV §4
50	  all state the quotient for orbits-in-affines with **no separatedness hypothesis**)
51	  handles stable non-affine overlaps via the *local nature of the affine quotient*:
52	  `π_U : U → Spec (Γ(U)^Γ)` is integral (each `s` kills `∏_γ (T - γ•s)`, a monic
53	  polynomial over `Γ(U)^Γ`) and its fibres are exactly the `Γ`-orbits (transitivity
54	  of the action on primes over a prime of the invariants — mathlib:
55	  `Algebra.IsInvariant` API), so a stable open `V ≤ U` has open image
56	  `π_U(V) = π_U(V ∖ ∅)` with `π_U⁻¹(π_U V) = V`, and `π_U(V)` is covered by
57	  invariant basic opens `D(N)`, `N ∈ Γ(U)^Γ` (the `StableAffineCover` norm trick run
58	  *inside the single chart* `U`, where it needs no separatedness), on which the

9	# The base divisor exists over every field, at every genus — the residue of
10	extension-uniformity is a degree bound and nothing else
11	
12	`UniformBaseDivisor C d` (`Ledger/ExtensionUniformity.lean`) is the single remaining input of
13	extension-uniform `H¹` vanishing
14	(`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.uniformVanishing_of_uniformBaseDivisor`).
15	It asks for **one** degree bound `d`, chosen before any field, such that over every
16	extension `κ/k` some divisor of degree `≤ d` already has vanishing `H¹`.
17	
18	Its two clauses have very different costs, and this file separates them, because the project's
19	own index for the gap does not.
20	
21	* **The existence clause is FREE, at every genus.**  `exists_base_subsingleton_baseChangeField`
22	  below: for **every** field extension `κ/k` there is a divisor `D₀` on `C_κ` with
23	  `H¹(𝒪(D₀)) = 0`.  Three curve binders, no genus hypothesis, no hypothesis on `κ/k`, one term.
24	* **The degree clause is the whole residue.**  Nothing here bounds `deg_κ D₀` as `κ` varies, and
25	  that — not the production of a vanishing divisor — is what `UniformBaseDivisor` still needs.
26	
27	## Why this is a re-pricing and not a restatement
28	
29	`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.lean:426-430` prices the gap as a missing **production from
30	geometry**: "For `UniformBaseDivisor` none [no producer] does: it is a `def` with consumers and
31	no producer anywhere in AJC", concluding "the gap is not a missing consumer or a carrier mismatch
32	— it is a missing production from geometry, and that is the form the next attempt should take."
33	That paragraph then records its own partial refutation: `Ledger/VanishingFieldDescent.lean`
34	produced `UniformBaseDivisor C 0`, but only under `Subsingleton (H¹(𝒪_C))`, which
35	`subsingleton_hModule_one_iff_genus_eq_zero` shows is exactly `genus C = 0`.  So the standing
36	picture is that `genus C ≥ 1` still awaits a production from geometry.
37	
38	That is measured here and it is wrong in a way worth naming: **the production from geometry
39	already exists, at every genus.**  `Ledger/FiberBound.exists_base_subsingleton_of_isFinite_toP1`
40	produces a vanishing divisor from a finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, and on AJC's curve the `π` and
41	both cohomology finiteness binders are theorems of the project
42	(`Ledger/MapToP1.exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1`, `Ledger/ChiCurve.lean`) — with no genus
43	hypothesis anywhere in that chain.  Applying it at `Scheme.baseChangeField C κ`, whose three
44	curve binders are witnessed by `ExtensionUniformity` §1, gives the existence clause over every
45	`κ` outright.
46	
47	The genus-0 restriction of `VanishingFieldDescent` is therefore a property of **that route** —
48	transporting the vanishing of the *unit* sheaf by faithful flatness, which forces the witness to
49	be the zero divisor and hence `H¹(𝒪_C)` itself to vanish — and not a property of the obligation.
50	The obligation never needed the unit sheaf.
51	
52	## What remains open, stated exactly
53	
54	One bound on one integer.  The divisor produced at `C_κ` is `n₀(κ) • F_κ`, where `F_κ` is the
55	fibre divisor of the finite dominant map to `ℙ¹_κ` and `n₀(κ)` is a Noetherian stabilisation
56	index of the fibre-lattice chain (`Ledger/FiberVanishing.lean`), re-run at each base field.  So
57	`deg_κ (n₀(κ) • F_κ) = n₀(κ) · deg_κ F_κ`, and `UniformBaseDivisor C d` follows from a uniform
58	bound on that product.  Nothing in this file bounds it, and the honest statement of the gap is
59	that product rather than "a missing production from geometry".
60	
61	The reason the bound is not free from the vanishing theorems already in the tree: the degree
62	threshold of `Ledger/DegreeVanishing.subsingleton_hModule_one_of_deg_ge` is
63	`deg D₀ + 1 − χ(𝒪)`, i.e. it is stated *relative to a base divisor already in hand*, so using it
64	to bound `deg D₀` is circular.  Breaking the circle needs an absolute large-degree vanishing
65	theorem — Serre duality's `deg ≥ 2g − 1`, which this workspace does not have — or a bound on the
66	stabilisation index in terms of `genus C`, which is base-field-invariant
67	(`Ledger/GenusFieldInvariance.genus_baseChangeField_curve`).
68	
69	**The second route is the live one, and `finrank_stabilisationAmbient_eq_h1` below is the
70	measurement that makes it concrete.**  `n₀(κ)` is produced by
71	`Submodule.eventually_eq_top_of_monotone_of_iSup_eq_top` from a monotone chain `Aₙ` inside
72	`N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`, and the quotient it stabilises in is *exactly* `H¹(𝒪(D + n·F))` — so at

79	statement of the remaining obligation is either strictness of `n ↦ Aₙ` below the top, or any other
80	argument bounding `n₀` by a base-field-invariant quantity.  This is *not* claimed here, and the

118	* `exists_base_subsingleton_curve` — over `k`, at every genus: a divisor with vanishing `H¹`.

129	-/

386	/-! ## The quotient predicate and the existence gate -/
387	
388	section Quotient
389	
390	variable {K L}
391	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
392	
393	/-- `(Y, g)` is a **finite Galois quotient** of the semilinearly-acted `(X, f, ρ)`
394	(campaign `G2`): there is an isomorphism `e : Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L ≅ X` which is
395	
396	1. over `Spec L`,
397	2. `Γ`-equivariant for the canonical base-change action, and
398	3. universal: every equivariant morphism `T ×_{Spec K} Spec L ⟶ X` over `Spec L`
399	   descends **uniquely** to `T ⟶ Y` over `Spec K` — this clause is exactly
400	   `Hom_K(T, Y) ≅ Hom_L(T_L, X)^Γ` (the inverse bijection direction is
401	   `SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackMap_comp`). -/
402	def IsGaloisQuotient (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
403	    (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) : Prop :=
404	  ∃ e : pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ≅ X,
405	    e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ∧
406	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).IsEquivariant ρ e.hom ∧
407	    ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
408	      (h : pullback t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X),
409	      h ≫ f = pullback.snd t (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) →
410	      (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L t).IsEquivariant ρ h →
411	      ∃! u : {u : T ⟶ Y // u ≫ g = t},
412	        pullbackBaseChange K L g t u.1 u.2 ≫ e.hom = h
413	
414	/-- GATE (campaign `G2`) — existence of the finite Galois quotient under the
415	orbit-in-affine hypothesis.
416	
417	**No longer instance-free, and the qualification matters: it is discharged on the
418	AFFINE locus** (`hasGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine`,
419	`Picard/GaloisQuotientAffineGeneral.lean`, a global `instance`), so for `[IsAffine X]`
420	this class synthesizes outright and subsumes the former single-object witness
421	`hasGaloisQuotient_specF4`. Both measurements below are **from a file importing that
422	module**, which this one is two hops below, so do not expect to reproduce either
423	here: `inferInstance` closes the `𝔽₄` goal, and — the other direction — **fails** for
424	an abstract `ρ` carrying the orbit hypothesis but not affineness, so the remaining
425	content is exactly the non-affine case.
426	
427	Intended discharge of what is left (`G2(c)`): a `Γ`-stable affine cover
428	(`HasStableAffineCover`, from `OrbitsInAffineOpen` via the EGA II 4.5.4 pattern),
429	`Spec (A_U^Γ)` on each stable affine piece by Speiser descent
430	(`SemilinearAlgebras.descentAlgEquiv` — the affine Hom property is
431	`affineGaloisQuotientHomEquiv` below; the per-chart *quotient* is now the affine
432	instance above rather than something to re-derive), glued via `Scheme.GlueData`.
433	The orbit hypothesis is **essential** for that step (Hironaka trap — module
434	docstring), and the affine discharge does not weaken it: an affine `X` has no room
435	for the trap. -/
436	class HasGaloisQuotient [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
437	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) [ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen] : Prop where
438	  exists_quotient :
439	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), IsGaloisQuotient ρ g
440	
441	end Quotient
442	
443	/-! ## The left-factor Galois action on `L ⊗[K] B` -/
444	
445	section TensorAction
446	
447	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra K B]
448	
449	/-- The left-factor Galois action `γ ↦ γ ⊗ id` on a base change `L ⊗[K] B`.
450	Scoped instance: mathlib carries no action of `L ≃ₐ[K] L` on tensor products, so no
451	diamond can arise; still scoped for hygiene since for `B = L` the *right*-factor
452	action is equally natural. -/
453	noncomputable scoped instance instMulSemiringActionTensor :
454	    MulSemiringAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (L ⊗[K] B) where
455	  smul γ x := Algebra.TensorProduct.map (γ : L →ₐ[K] L) (AlgHom.id K B) x
456	  one_smul x := by
457	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x = x
458	    rw [show ((1 : L ≃ₐ[K] L) : L →ₐ[K] L) = AlgHom.id K L from rfl,
459	      Algebra.TensorProduct.map_id, AlgHom.coe_id, id_eq]
460	  mul_smul γ τ x := by
461	    change Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x
462	      = Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ (Algebra.TensorProduct.map _ _ x)
463	    rw [← AlgHom.comp_apply, ← Algebra.TensorProduct.map_comp]
464	    rfl
465	  smul_zero γ := map_zero _
466	  smul_add γ := map_add _
467	  smul_one γ := map_one _
468	  smul_mul γ := map_mul _
